bug_semantics: Renovate's gradle-wrapper manager invokes the wrapper update command through a shell (`/bin/sh -c ... ./gradlew :wrapper --gradle-distribution-url <value>`), interpolating the repository-supplied `distributionUrl` from gradle-wrapper.properties directly into the command string without quoting. A repository with a malicious gradle-wrapper.properties whose distributionUrl contains shell command substitution (e.g. `$(...)`) gets that text evaluated by the shell before Gradle parses the URL, yielding arbitrary command execution in the Renovate runtime (CWE-78), even when allowScripts/toolConstraints gating would otherwise apply.
flaw_origin: Commit 969d455a3c9b97fb874e4fd11ec30cbc2c354304 ("fix(gradle-wrapper): use distribution url instead of version (#6003)", 2020-04-19, author Rhys Arkins <rhys@arkins.net>, committer GitHub, no AI trailers) introduced `getDistributionUrl(newPackageFileContent)` — parsing distributionUrl out of the repository's gradle-wrapper.properties — and appended it into the shell command: `cmd += ' --gradle-distribution-url ${distributionUrl}'` unquoted, inside the string-command pipeline executed via exec. The advisory's named sink (distributionUrl evaluated by the shell) is born here; before this commit the command interpolated only config.toVersion (5e56a9aacaf, #5842) and never the raw properties file value. The later refactor 8586f463ea0 (2022-08-16) preserved the same unquoted interpolation line (`cmd += ' --gradle-distribution-url ${distributionUrl}'`), recorded as a persistence wave.
